props.covers: Overview and index of the seven-stage worked example: one board built through section-skeleton, per-section content, connection, and review batches, with fresh board digests, local deltas, cumulative board diffs, lint changes, routed truth, request status, and painted-extent renders.

text.insert: A board in seven edits
A small runner-and-score board grows through ordered
apply_ops

calls against one session draft, grouped into seven incremental instructions. For each instruction, the model studies the latest pushed digest and render, sends the complete section skeleton needed by that instruction, fills one section per batch while judging each result, adds connections after the nodes exist, and reviews bottom-up. Each page shows the ordered JSON call payloads for that stage and the frozen board illustration after it. The harness validates each whole batch before mutation, snaps geometry to the 16px grid, reconciles section membership from geometry, auto-fits affected sections, and routes connections. The fresh BOARD digest, DELTA, lint state, and renders tell the model what actually happened. The
rulebook

reference.label: The layout rulebook: corpus rules R1-R10

text.insert: documents how the named R1-R10 concerns are owned by the aesthetic, operation mechanics, and diagnostics.
The seven steps
Step 1 — A lane and a stage

reference.label: Step 1 — A lane and a stage

text.insert: — establish the Config and Stage sections first, then add three stacked pills and a placeholder sticky.
Step 2 — The runner pipeline
— replace the placeholder stage with four evenly spaced runner nodes ending in a decision.
Step 3 — The board hub below
— trim and move the runner row upward, then add a Board — hub section with three database stores.
Step 4 — A score column
— add the Score gate section, reflow the existing bands, and build its three-node vertical chain.
Step 5 — Review the hero row
— use an empty batch with view to examine the Score gate without mutating the board, and judge whether the intended shared centerline reads clearly.
Step 6 — Fan out, wire the arrows

reference.label: Step 6 — Fan out, wire the arrows

text.insert: — compact the score chain and add two outcome pills, judge that render, then add ten routed connections after all endpoints exist.
Step 7 — The edit: one more store

reference.label: Step 7 — The edit: one more store

text.insert: — explicitly reposition the three stores into a 2x2 arrangement, add cache, review the routed consequence, and finalize the cumulative proposal.
How pushed results show locality

Every successful edit batch and pure look carries a fresh BOARD digest. Each accepted batch also separates DELTA—the before-to-after changes from this call—from BOARD DIFF, the cumulative baseline-to-draft operations a committed finalize proposes. That makes locality explicit. A structural stage such as
step 4
moves and resizes whole bands through a skeleton batch followed by one content batch per touched section.
step 5
is a pure look: its empty DELTA and fresh BOARD digest accompany a section close-up and no fresh full-board render.
step 7

reference.label: Step 7 — The edit: one more store

text.insert: changes only the hub stores and the route affected by the moved saves endpoint, while the cumulative BOARD DIFF still carries the entire seven-step proposal.
